findings.title: CustomerService::show() missing target-role guard — read-side privilege escalation (any User id leaks PII)
findings.evidence: The WAVE5-SEC-001 heal added assertTargetRole() to update() (CustomerService.php:98), changePassword() (:196) and changeImage() (:218) to block mutating non-Customer Users. But show() (:128-140) was NOT given the same guard: it only checks `!in_array(EnumRole::CUSTOMER, $this->blockRoles)` which is a constant tautology (blockRoles=[ADMIN], so CUSTOMER is never in it → always true) and returns the route-bound User as-is. Route GET /customer/show/{customer} (routes/api.php:547) implicit-binds ANY User (no Route::bind role scoping — grep confirmed none) and is gated only by `permission:customers_show` (CustomerController.php:39). CustomerResource (CustomerResource.php:20-31) then returns name/email/phone/username. So a Branch-Manager/partial staffer holding customers_show can pass an Admin or staff user id and read their PII. The same read-side asymmetry exists on myOrder (OrderService::userOrder filters only `where('user_id',$user->id)`, OrderService.php:253-254, gated by permission:customers) and on address index (CustomerAddressController.php:25).
findings.why_it_matters: Direct read-side of the exact horizontal/vertical escalation that WAVE5-SEC-001 patched on the write side. The mutator/reader asymmetry is strong code evidence this is an oversight, not intent. Leaks staff/admin email+phone (PII / GDPR-relevant) to any operator with the read permission.
findings.reproduction: As a user with role granting only `customers_show` (e.g. Branch Manager), call GET /api/admin/customer/show/{id} with an Admin or Chef user id. Code path returns that user's CustomerResource (PII). Live-verify needs a non-admin role actually holding customers_show.
findings.recommended_correction: Add `$this->assertTargetRole($customer);` at the top of CustomerService::show() (mirror update/changePassword/changeImage). Apply equivalently before OrderService::userOrder() use in CustomerController::myOrder and before address index, OR scope the {customer} route binding to the Customer role via Route::bind / a scoped implicit binding.

findings.title: Customer address write ops (store/update/destroy) gated by a READ permission (customers_show)
findings.evidence: Constructor middleware: `$this->middleware(['permission:customers_show'])->only('index','store','update','destroy','show');`. The mutating endpoints POST /customer/address/{customer}, PUT/PATCH /customer/address/{customer}/{address}, DELETE /customer/address/{customer}/{address} (routes/api.php:559-561) are therefore authorised by the *read* permission customers_show — not customers_create/customers_edit/customers_delete, which exist as distinct, separately-assignable permissions (PermissionTableSeeder.php:475-499; CustomerController.php:36-38 uses the granular trio for its own CRUD).
findings.why_it_matters: Least-privilege violation / inconsistency: an operator granted only view access to customers can create, modify and delete their delivery addresses (affecting delivery routing / DeliveryQuoteService geocode). The sibling CustomerController already models the correct granular gating, so this is an internal inconsistency.
findings.reproduction: Assign a role only `customers_show`. POST /api/admin/customer/address/{customer} succeeds (address created) though the role lacks any *_create/_edit/_delete customer permission.
findings.recommended_correction: Split the gates: keep customers_show on index/show; gate store with customers_create (or a new customers_edit), update with customers_edit, destroy with customers_delete — matching CustomerController.php:36-38.

findings.title: ProfileChangePasswordComponent success toast: dead `?? 0` and boolean passed where flip-index expected
findings.evidence: `alertService.successFlip(res.config.method === "put" ?? 0, this.$t("menu.password"))`. `res.config.method === "put"` is always a boolean (true/false), so the `?? 0` nullish-coalescing branch is unreachable dead code (a boolean is never null/undefined). successFlip(status=null,...) (alertService.js:48) expects status to select created-vs-updated wording; it receives `true`/`false` instead of an id/0. Operator-precedence: `===` binds tighter than `??`, so this parses as `(method==='put') ?? 0`.
findings.why_it_matters: Minor: the change-password confirmation toast may show the wrong created/updated variant, and the code carries a misleading dead operand. Cosmetic only; password change itself works.
findings.reproduction: Admin > Profile > Change Password, submit valid form; inspect the toast wording / pass a boolean into successFlip.
findings.recommended_correction: Drop the `?? 0` and pass an explicit flip value, e.g. `alertService.successFlip(1, this.$t('menu.password'))` (a password change is always an update), consistent with ProfileEditProfileComponent.vue:142 which uses `successFlip(1, ...)`.

findings.title: Subscriber broadcast email sent synchronously to all subscribers in one BCC, no queue/chunk
findings.evidence: sendEmail() does `$subscribers = Subscriber::pluck('email');` then `Mail::bcc($subscribers->toArray())->send(new SubscriberMail(...))` — a single synchronous send over the whole subscriber base, inside the HTTP request (SubscriberController::sendEmail:57-61). No ShouldQueue, no chunking, no per-recipient send.
findings.why_it_matters: As the subscriber list grows the request blocks until the SMTP transaction completes (or times out → 422). A single BCC to many recipients also raises deliverability/spam-filtering risk and exposes the whole list to one transport failure (all-or-nothing). For V1 Le Cayenne single-resto the list is small so impact is low today, hence P3.
findings.reproduction: POST /api/admin/subscriber/send-email with a large Subscriber table; the request latency scales with the mail transaction and can hit the request timeout.
findings.recommended_correction: Queue the mail (implement ShouldQueue on SubscriberMail or dispatch a job) and chunk recipients (e.g. Subscriber::chunk(200) → queued Mail::to() per recipient), so the controller returns immediately and one bad address doesn't fail the whole batch.

solids.title: Customer = branch_id=0 User, exempt from BranchScope intentionally (task hint satisfied)
solids.note: BranchScope::apply early-returns for `$model instanceof User` to avoid Sanctum guard re-entry/recursion (documented at :19-20). Customers are User rows seeded with branch_id=0, so they are deliberately not branch-filtered. The sentinel's `App\Models\Customer` exemption (BranchScopeCoverageSentinelTest:51) is a separate model; the User exemption is the relevant one here. Intentional and documented — not a defect.

solids.title: WAVE5-SEC-001 target-role guard correctly protects the three customer mutators
solids.note: assertTargetRole() throws HttpException(403) if the route-bound User is not a Customer, placed BEFORE the try/catch so the 403 survives QueryExceptionLibrary rewrap. Blocks a customers_edit holder from rotating an Admin's password via PUT /customer/{anyUserId}. Correct (the read-side gap in S10-01 is the remaining hole).

solids.title: Admin self-service password change verifies the old password; admin reset path correctly omits it
solids.note: ProfileController self-change uses ChangePasswordRequest whose withValidator/checkOldPassword (Hash::check against auth user) enforces old_password — so ProfileService::changePassword not re-checking it is fine (enforced at the FormRequest layer). The admin-reset-a-customer path (UserChangePasswordRequest) intentionally omits old_password (admin doesn't know it) and requires min:12 letters+numbers + confirmed. Both correct.

solids.title: Address IDOR protection: ownership asserted on update/destroy/show
solids.note: update/destroy/show all guard `if ($user->id == $address->user_id)` else throw, so a mismatched {customer}/{address} pair in the route cannot mutate or read another user's address. Prevents the cross-record IDOR the nested route shape would otherwise allow.

solids.title: route('X.id') dot-notation in FormRequests resolves correctly (NOT a bug — verified)
solids.note: Verified via tinker: Route::parameter -> Arr::get supports dot notation and the bound User implements ArrayAccess, so Arr::get(['customer'=>$user],'customer.id') returns the user's id (printed int(1)), and null on create (store, no param). Thus Rule::unique()->ignore(id) excludes the current row on update and password becomes nullable on update / required on create — exactly as intended. Same pattern across all sibling *Request classes. Recorded as a SOLID to pre-empt a false-positive.
